title: Dissociation of intact adult mouse cortical projection neurons for single-cell RNA-seq
protocol: Euthanize mice (postnatal day 28 and older, male and female) with isoflurane using the open drop method.
Transcardially perfuse with cold, carbogenated aCSF for 3 min at a rate of 3.75 ml/min.
Dissect out the entire brain and place it in one of the petri dishes filled with aCSF continuously bubbled with carbogen on ice for 3 min.
Place the cold brain in the adult brain matrix.
Cut 500 μm thick sections through primary motor cortex using a fresh razor blade.
Immediately place sections in cold carbogenated aCSF under the epifluorescent dissecting microscope.
Macro dissect the regions of interest based on the location of fluorescent cell bodies.
Transfer dissected tissue to 5 mL microfuge tubes containing 3 mL enzyme solution (dissociation buffer + Papain).
Place 5 mL tubes on an orbital shaker in an incubation oven set to 34°C.
Remove papain solution with a P1000 pipette, allowing the tissue chunks to remain at the bottom of the tube.
Add 2 mL of Stop solution and place on ice.
Incubate the solution for 5 minutes without shaking or mixing.
Remove stop solution with a P1000 pipette.
Replace with 800 μL of cold dissociation buffer.
Triturate sample with fire-polished pipettes starting with a diameter of 600 μm, tritrate 10 times.
Triturate 10 times with the pipette of 300 μm diameter.
Triturate 6 times with the pipette of 150 μm diameter.
Place samples on ice until ready for FACS.
Add a drop of 8 μm–12.9 μm polystyrene particle standard beads into 1× PBS.
Add a drop of 13 μm–17.9 μm polystyrene particle standard beads into 1× PBS.
Sort the bead solution with forward scatter area and back scatter area to establish the first gate.
Set the size gate of the sample based on the beads size.
Use backscatter height and width to remove cellular doublets or intact cells plus debris.
Use a non-fluorescent control sample to set the fluorescence gate (tdTomato from reporter mouse).
Collect intact cells expressing tdTomato and enriched in cytoplasmic dye.
Add cytoplasmic dye directly to the sample at a concentration of 1:1000.
Gently flick tube to mix into solution.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Spin cells at 300 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant with a P1000 pipette without disturbing the loose pellet.
Resuspend in 500 μL dissociation buffer using a P1000 pipette carefully.
Run the resuspended cell solution through a 35 μm nylon mesh cap to remove debris.
Load the nonfluorescent sample incubated with cytoplasmic dye into the sorter.
Set gates based on backscatter width and height to exclude doublets.
Sort cells based on far-red (cytoplasmic dye) and tdTomato fluorescence.
Draw a gate selecting for intact fluorescent neurons: tdTomato high, far-red high.
Use a negative control sample to set initial sorting parameters if needed.
Sort the samples using previously determined gates.
Sort samples directly into a microfuge tube containing 500 μL of cold dissociation buffer for 10X sequencing or other droplet-based sequencing methods.
Proceed immediately to the sequencing step after sorting.
Spin down collected cells at 500g for 5 minutes if using 10X sequencing method.
Very carefully remove most of the supernatant and load all cells in 34 μL of cold dissociation buffer into the chromium chip.
Sort samples directly into the plate if using plate-based sequencing.
Sort up to 5 × 10^5 cells into 350 μL of lysis buffer for qPCR.
Sort cells directly into a 96-well plate containing fixative solution for immunocytochemistry.
Sort cells into 20 μL of warm media per 10,000 cells sorted for long-term tissue culture.
Add 100 μL of warm media along with the sorted cells to each well of a 0.01% poly-D-lysine- and 10 μg/mL laminin-coated 24-well plate.
Plate 30,000 cells per well for best results in long-term tissue culture.
Allow sorted cells to adhere for 30 minutes.
Remove media after adherence to remove debris.
Replace with 500 μL of warm media and maintain cells with 50% media replacement every other day.
